newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended higher on Monday but well off today's peaks reversing the negative trend of the three previous sessions.
A stronger peseta was supporting bonds, as dealers eyed U.S. data, due tomorrow, for hints on future dollar trends.
On Tuesday, U.S. fourth quarter employment cost is due at 1330 GMT and consumer confidence at 1500 GMT.
"If the dollar and the peseta are strong against the mark, we can have a decoupling between US and European rates," said Henrik Lumholdt, economist at Bank of America in Madrid.
"The only thing we really care about for tomorrow are the American data, which offer us a clue about future U.S. inflation and the possible trend in interest rates," said a dealer in Madrid.
The 10-year cash spread over Bunds declined a bit ending at 91 basis points, from 93 bps at Friday's evening, while the differential under US notes was trading at minus three bps.
The Spanish yield curve was virtually unchanged.
The 9.4 percent April 1999 bond ended at 108.33, yielding 5.33 pct from 5.34 at the start this morning.
The two- to 10-year spread widened to 137 bps from 136 bps.
